title: ERL2 environment driver, clean-control, frontier and substrate-lock contracts
$comment: Design v2 §9/§12/§22 and implementation plan §9. No contract here names a product or a subject-supported evidence class: source kinds are open identifiers owned by the environment contract (ERL2-FR-002).

EnvironmentDriverManifestV1.$comment: A driver is admissible only when `enabled` is true. The Compose driver stays disabled while its substrate lock is unqualified (ERL2-OQ-005).

allOf.$comment: A disabled driver must state why and name its activation gate; an enabled driver may not carry either field.
A Compose driver is only admissible against a qualified substrate lock.

SubstrateLockV1.$comment: ERL2-OQ-005. Qualification requires the archive digest, per-platform image digests, SBOM and provenance, and config hashes, all re-verified before an attesting run.

allOf.$comment: A qualified lock requires at least one image digest, an SBOM and provenance, and forbids an unqualified reason.

EnvironmentResourceV1.$comment: Every resource identity embeds the run id, so cleanup can never target a foreign resource (design v2 §22).

EnvironmentOperationReceiptV1.$comment: Every external mutation is intent -> receipt -> event -> snapshot. A receipt carries before/after state and a compensation identifier where one applies.

EnvironmentBaselineFingerprintV1.$comment: The clean control. `fingerprint_hash` is derived from the ordered probe observations only, so two clean provisions of the same archetype produce identical bytes.

EnvironmentResourceFrontierV1.$comment: Frozen before emergency cleanup. The safe-action set is derived independently from the frontier, never supplied by the driver (ERL2-FR-025).

EnvironmentReservationLeaseV1.$comment: The global allocator stores reservation leases only — never resource state (design v2 §22).

ChallengeActivationReceiptV1.$comment: Signed controller evidence that the selected challenge was activated in the provisioned environment (design v2 §12 'activate/start/cutoff: signed controller and traffic receipts'). Additive contract ERL2-C-155 (ADR-ERL2-023); no existing schema changed. The controller is a separated role: the driver's own EnvironmentOperationReceiptV1 records what the substrate did and carries no signature, so it cannot attest who authorized the activation.

SubstrateBindingV1.$comment: Signed Lab evidence binding one run permanently to one substrate identity (ADR-ERL2-024 §4.2). Additive contract ERL2-C-156; no existing schema changed shape or meaning. It exists because `--substrate-root` was caller-controlled, ungated, and bound into no contract, no receipt and no attestation field, so a caller could drive the environment against substrate A and then destroy and finalize against a fresh empty substrate B, obtaining an offline-valid attestation while the real environment stayed allocated (review P0-1). The canonical identity is `substrate_instance_hash`, a value the substrate itself carries: a fresh substrate has none, which is what makes substitution detectable offline. The operational locator is deliberately ABSENT — a path is deployment-local, unstable across hosts, unverifiable by a reader who has no path to hash, and would bake an absolute host path into signed public evidence; it is kept in the run's private `state/` subtree instead. Signed by the environment governor, never by the driver: a driver is untrusted infrastructure and must not attest its own substrate identity.

ObservedResourceIdentity.$comment: One resource as the substrate reported it at a single moment: the driver's own resource id and the identity hash that derives from its run-scoped name. Both are retained because the two answer different questions — the id keys the derived actions, the identity hash keys the residue accounting.

CleanupResidueProbeV1.$comment: Lab evidence that the substrate was independently re-observed after the last cleanup dispatch (ADR-ERL2-027 §4.3). Additive contract ERL2-C-158; no existing schema changed shape or meaning. It exists because `EmergencyCleanupVerificationV1.remaining_resources` is derived by the producer from the producer's own action outcomes — so a cleanup that marked every action `succeeded` produced an empty residue that nothing offline could contradict, and a resource that vanished with no authorized action was undetectable (review P1-1, and §1.6). `observed_before` restates the pre-action frontier so a probe built over a post-destruction inventory is refused; `observed_after` is the observation nothing retained before; `authorized_targets` is the derived safe-action target set. `outcome` is derived from those three and is never supplied. Unsigned: an invalid terminal emits no attestation and no public bundle, so there is no external reader a signature would serve.

substrate_binding_hash.$comment: The binding of ADR-ERL2-024 §4.2. A probe naming another run's substrate observed another environment.

resource_frontier_hash.$comment: The pre-action frontier this probe closes over. The expectation must come from the frontier frozen before the first dispatch, never from an inventory reconstructed after one.

observed_before.$comment: The substrate as the frontier observed it, before any cleanup dispatch. Restated here so the probe stands alone and so a probe assembled over a later observation disagrees with the frontier it names.

observed_after.$comment: The substrate re-observed after the last cleanup dispatch. This is the observation the verdict comes from, and the one that did not exist before this contract.

authorized_targets.$comment: Resource ids the derived safe actions authorized a dispatch against. Anything absent afterwards that is not in this set disappeared without the Lab authorizing it.

undeclared_destroyed_resources.$comment: Resources present before, absent after, and never authorized. Non-empty is a Lab-integrity failure regardless of cause: the Lab cannot account for an effect it did not authorize.

residual_resources.$comment: Frontier members still observed afterwards. This is what `EmergencyCleanupVerificationV1.remaining_resources` must agree with, and the reason it is now checkable.

probe_status.$comment: `unavailable` when the substrate could not be re-observed. Fail-closed, not a pass: a cleanup that cannot be observed cannot be claimed complete.

outcome.$comment: Derived from the sets above, never supplied. `clean` is the only one that supports a complete cleanup; `undeclared_destruction` is the offline-detectable form of destroy-first-classify-afterwards.

ExpectedRevertedMutation.$comment: One mutation the compensation was expected to reverse, tied to the retained receipt that recorded it being applied and to the resource it was applied to.

RestorationProbeV1.$comment: Signed Lab evidence that the substrate was independently re-read after a compensation (ADR-ERL2-026 §4). Additive contract ERL2-C-157; no existing schema changed shape or meaning. It exists because restoration was derived from the before/after baseline fingerprints, the residual resource set and the compensation receipt's own `status` — none of which can see a mutation. A driver that returned `status: "succeeded"` and reverted nothing produced `passed: true` over a mutation that was still applied, and 'reverted nothing' was indistinguishable from 'had nothing to revert' (review P1-4). `expected_reverted_mutations` names, from durable pre-compensation intent, exactly what the compensation was supposed to undo, and `observed_after` is what the substrate itself reported afterwards. `outcome` is derived from those two sets and is never asserted. Signed by the environment governor for the same reason the substrate binding is: the driver is untrusted infrastructure and must not be the authority on whether its own compensation worked.

substrate_binding_hash.$comment: The binding of §4.2. A probe that names another run's substrate is a probe of another environment.

compensation_operation_id.$comment: The operation the receipt below belongs to. Pins a receipt to the compensation it is cited for, so a stale receipt replayed from another operation cannot stand in.

expected_reverted_mutations.$comment: What the compensation was declared to revert, one entry per retained mutation receipt. Empty only when the run applied no mutation at all — which is what makes 'reverted nothing' and 'had nothing to revert' different outcomes rather than the same silence.

observed_before.$comment: Mutation ids the substrate reported applied immediately before the compensation was dispatched. On a resumed run whose compensation already completed this is legitimately empty; it is evidence, not a precondition.

observed_after.$comment: Mutation ids the substrate reported applied after the compensation, read back independently. This is the observation the verdict comes from.

residual_expected_mutations.$comment: Expected mutations still present in `observed_after`. Non-empty is a restoration failure whatever the receipt claimed.

collateral_reverted_mutations.$comment: Mutations present before that were removed without being expected. A compensation that reverted unrelated state did not restore the environment either, and must not be reported as if it had.

probe_status.$comment: `unavailable` when the driver offers no applied-mutation observation. It is a fail-closed outcome, not a pass: a restoration that cannot be observed cannot be claimed.

outcome.$comment: Derived from the sets above, never supplied. `reverted` and `nothing_to_revert` are the only two that support a valid terminal, and they are deliberately distinct.

AttributableTelemetryObservationV1.$comment: ADR-ERL2-033: telemetry the run's own collector actually received, attributable to this run by its marker — the run id itself. Discriminated evidence in the ADR-ERL2-016 sense: only `observed` may carry counts, a collector identity or the log excerpt, and no field stores a verdict. 'Attributable telemetry was received' is derivable only from an `observed` record whose `run_attributed_records` is positive, by the producer's validity gate and the offline verifier independently — the verifier recomputes every count from the retained excerpt's bytes. The observation post-dates the realized evidence cutoff by construction (the exercising step runs after `observe`), so it backs no claim inside the frozen evidence window and never touches the source snapshots' `records: 0`.

marker.$comment: The string whose occurrences in the collector's own output count as run-attributed records. The gate and the verifier both require it to equal `run_id`: the expected marker is re-derivable by every reader, never a subject-shaped free variable.

evidence.$comment: Only `observed` can contribute to any positive statement (ADR-ERL2-016 decision 2, applied here by ADR-ERL2-033 decision 2).

collector.$comment: The exact container the logs were read from, as Docker proved it — the observed identity, never the lock's expectation. The driver refuses to read an unverified container's logs, so an unverified observation is unrepresentable as `observed`: both proof booleans are schema constants.

log_excerpt.$comment: The collector-log lines every count above is derived from, kept inline and hash-covered rather than as a second retained file: the observation freezes before the lifecycle event that anchors it, and two files cannot be frozen atomically — a crash between them would leave either an excerpt no artifact references or an artifact referencing absent bytes, both of which the offline accounting refuses. Inline, one freeze carries both, and the verifier re-parses this string to recompute every count. Bounded: a collector output that exceeds the bound yields an `absent` observation with a reason code, never a truncated excerpt, because a truncated excerpt would derive counts that are not the run's.

allOf.$comment: Only an observation may carry counts, a collector identity or an excerpt; an `absent` record claiming any of them would be exactly the conflation ADR-ERL2-033 exists to prevent, so the schema makes it unrepresentable. Anything that is not an observation must say why.

AttributableTelemetryObservationV2.$comment: ADR-ERL2-038 §3 and corrections R2–R8: the trusted-telemetry artifact, and the ONLY format authoritative for a new telemetry claim. Where v1 derived counts from a mixed console stream whose framing a subject could reproduce byte for byte, v2 derives them structurally from newline-delimited OTLP JSON written by the collector's own file exporter, where a record boundary is not expressible in subject bytes. v1 (ERL2-C-160) stays registered and parseable so historical evidence keeps verifying under its original scope, and is refused for every new claim — absence or invalidity of v2 is a refusal, never a downgrade (R8). The trusted channel itself does not exist yet: this contract is package 1, the collector and volume are package 2, and the driver and live freeze are package 3, so no artifact of this shape has been produced by a collector.

marker.$comment: The run-attribution token, required to equal `run_id` by both the producer gate and the offline verifier, exactly as in v1: a marker a reader cannot re-derive attributes nothing.

evidence.$comment: Only `observed` can carry counts, bytes or identities (ADR-ERL2-016 decision 2). An `observed` record whose `record_count` is zero is an authentic observed zero — the channel was provisioned, finalized and empty — and is a different fact from `absent`, which says the channel produced nothing readable and must say why.

channel.$comment: Trusted-channel identity (R3). Every field is a schema constant except the exporter id, so a record whose bytes came from the mixed debug stream, from a rotated file, or from any format other than newline-delimited OTLP JSON is unrepresentable rather than merely refused.

rotation.$comment: R6: forbidden for the bounded MVP. One run-scoped artifact, one segment. A segmented design would need an ordered integrity-bound manifest and its own amendment.

binding.$comment: R4: the identities that make another run's artifact unusable here. Recomputed by the verifier against the run's own retained archetype, substrate lock and collector identity, so an artifact lifted from a different run, a different substrate or a different collector configuration cannot satisfy this one.

collector.$comment: Carried forward from v1 unchanged: the exact container the bytes were read from, as Docker proved it. Both proof booleans stay schema constants, so an unverified observation is unrepresentable as `observed`.

artifact.$comment: R5: the finalization proof, carried in the record rather than asserted by the producer. `byte_length` and `content_digest` are recomputed by the verifier over `trusted_records` itself, so the bytes the counts derive from are the bytes whose digest is retained; `record_count` is recomputed by parsing them. `final_record_terminated` states whether the byte sequence ends on a record boundary, and must be false exactly when the artifact is empty — a non-empty artifact that does not terminate is a partial write and fails closed.

finalization.$comment: A writing, crashed or unfinalized channel yields an `absent` record with a reason code. `frozen` is the only state an authoritative artifact may be in, so the alternatives are unrepresentable here rather than merely refused downstream.

trusted_records.$comment: The exact newline-delimited OTLP-JSON bytes every count above derives from, retained inline and hash-covered for the same reason v1's excerpt was: the observation freezes before the lifecycle event that anchors it, and two files cannot be frozen atomically. Bounded at the same 262144 ceiling, and made achievable at that ceiling by R2 — the trusted pipeline minimizes fields before export, so a record carries a bounded allowlist rather than whatever a subject attached. Subject-derived values are not absent from these bytes: they may appear inside the allowlisted marker-bearing field, JSON-escaped and length-bounded, and nowhere else.

allOf.$comment: The v1 discrimination, extended to the new identity and integrity blocks: only an observation may carry a channel, a binding, a collector, an artifact, counts or bytes, and anything that is not an observation must say why. `log_excerpt` is absent from `properties` and `additionalProperties` is false, so a record mixing v1 and v2 fields fails the schema itself rather than a downstream check.
